What I went through with Lipton is not just a simple product error—it is a series of negligence, poor handling, and a complete failure in customer care. I purchased a product clearly labeled as “cardamom-flavored,” yet the contents inside had nothing to do with that flavor. This is not merely a flavor issue—it’s a matter of credibility.

As one of the biggest names in the global tea market, I expected Lipton to treat the issue with seriousness and urgency. Instead, I faced long delays, cold responses, and an eventual “solution” that had no connection to the original problem. Sending a box of plain tea in place of the actual item I paid for is not a solution—it’s an insult to the consumer's intelligence.

An apology, while appreciated, means nothing without real action. Apologizing without truly fixing the problem is just a polished front that resolves nothing. And to offer a product that doesn’t match the original issue as some kind of compensation? That shows a clear disregard for the customer's experience.

Through this experience, Lipton has proven that it has abandoned the most basic standards of customer service and respect for loyal buyers. The trust they once enjoyed wasn’t handed to them—it was earned over time. And now, they’ve thrown it away carelessly.

Let me be very clear: I no longer trust your products, I will not consume them again, and I will make sure my experience is publicly shared so others know how easily a “big brand” can become a major disappointment in the eyes of its customers.
